papers.title: Learning from the Test: Self-Referential Differential Testing for Deep RL Agents
papers.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has achieved significant success in complex decision-making problems. As DRL systems are increasingly deployed in real-world applications, ensuring their quality and reliability is paramount. Current works primarily focus on detecting safety-critical failures, often neglecting policy optimality, which can lead to reduced efficiency, user distrust, and economic losses. papers.title: GrandTour: A legged robotics dataset in the wild for multi-modal perception and state estimation
papers.summary: Accurate state estimation and multi-modal perception are prerequisites for autonomous legged robots in complex, large-scale environments. To date, no large-scale public legged-robot dataset captures the real-world conditions needed to develop and benchmark algorithms for legged-robot state estimation, perception, and navigation. To address this, we introduce the GrandTour dataset, a multi-modal legged-robotics dataset collected across challenging outdoor and indoor environments, featuring an ANYbotics ANYmal-D quadruped equipped with the Boxi multi-modal sensor payload. papers.title: Optimizing and evaluating proximal policy optimization and soft actor-critic agents in Unity ML-Agents-based games
papers.summary: This study presents a comparative analysis of proximal policy optimization (PPO) and soft actor-critic (SAC) for training autonomous delivery agents in high-fidelity 3D environments using Unity ML-Agents. Both algorithms were evaluated with identical hyperparameters and reward functions across five independent runs to ensure statistical robustness. Results show that PPO achieves 31.4% higher final reward (6658.82 versus 5067.27) and superior policy improvement consistency (ratio 2.00 versus 0.31). papers.title: A neuromodulable current-mode silicon neuron for robust and adaptive neuromorphic systems
papers.summary: Abstract Neuromorphic engineering makes use of mixed-signal analog and digital circuits to directly emulate the computational principles of biological brains. Such electronic systems offer a high degree of adaptability, robustness, and energy efficiency across a wide range of tasks, from edge computing to robotics. Within this context, we investigate a key feature of biological neurons: their ability to carry out robust and reliable computation by adapting their input responses and spiking patterns to context through neuromodulation. papers.title: Human-robot coordination during hand-over tasks in virtual reality
papers.summary: Recent advancements in robotics have increased the integration of robotic systems into workplaces, necessitating effective human-robot collaboration. This thesis investigates human-robot coordination during handover tasks using Virtual Reality (VR) to analyze motor control and task dynamics across robot movement configurations. A behavioral study compared a repetitive pick-and-place task performed in physical and VR environments, establishing baseline differences. papers.title: OpenWater Hub: An open-source hardware platform for marine robotics support and water quality data acquisition
papers.summary: Marine environmental research often suffers from hardware fragmentation, requiring separate, incompatible systems for laboratory testing, portable field analysis, and long-term offshore monitoring. This increases costs and complicates data integration. This paper presents the OpenWater Hub, a versatile, open- source hardware platform that merges these functions into a single, reconfigurable electronics board. papers.title: Replanning human–robot collaborative tasks with vision–language models via semantic and physical dual–correction
papers.summary: Human–robot collaborative assembly requires robots to interpret ambiguous corrective instructions while producing physically executable motions. Vision–language models (VLMs) provide semantic reasoning but may select logically inconsistent targets or misjudge execution outcomes. We propose a replanning framework that maps human instructions to Action Target candidates, including grasp position and tool selections, and combines an Internal Correction Model for pre-execution logical verification with an External Correction Model for post-execution visual verification. papers.title: Design, prototype and control of a 3R1T robot with RCM for eye surgery
papers.summary: Minimally invasive surgery has significantly improved patient outcomes but, access to ophthalmic procedures such as cataract surgery remains constrained by high skill requirements and a limited number of surgeons. Eye surgery is particularly challenging due to physiological tremor, limited dexterity, and the fulcrum effect, which compromise precision. Robotic systems incorporating a remote centre of motion (RCM) can stabilise instruments and enhance precision, yet robotic eye surgery remains an unsolved challenge. papers.title: Reachability based planning for robotic manipulators
papers.summary: In the domain of modern robotics there still exist challenges in control on arguably one of the most fundamental levels, that is motion control. Since the 1980s there has been research into how to take advantage of the system dynamics of robots to provide better methods for motion control. In this thesis we explore the problem of providing control strategies to produce motions on robots, with formal guarantees of safety. papers.title: Worldbuilders: towards a dramaturgy of metaplasticity: affecting embodied change through immersive audio and story
papers.summary: In this thesis I propose a Dramaturgy of Metaplasticity. Metaplasticity is the dynamic and relational system consisting of body, mind and environment, an extended idea of neuroplasticity which suggests that change can be achieved in the body through the manipulation of the environment. This is enacted by drawing attention to the embodied self’s co-creative dynamic with its immediate environment. papers.title: Reconfigurable intelligent surface and UAV-assisted communications: a deep reinforcement learning approach
papers.summary: This thesis proposes novel methods based on the deep reinforcement learning algorithms (DRL) for maximising the energy efficiency (EE), sum-rate in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) and unmanned aerieal vehicles (UAV)-aided wireless communications. The thesis carries out comprehensive optimization and evaluation of various DRL algorithms for several real-life applications including UAV's trajectory design, power allocation, data collection, wireless power transfer and RIS's phase shift matrix adjustment. papers.title: Development and validation of VentPilot: an AI-based recommendation system for mechanical ventilation
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: Mechanical ventilation requires repeated adjustment to changing patient physiology, but consistent individualized management remains challenging. We developed VentPilot, an artificial intelligence-based system for recommending ventilator settings, and evaluated it in multicenter retrospective validation cohorts. papers.summary: The potential for active nano-electronic devices based on the creation and manipulation of pseudo-2D electrically conducting interfaces, such as domain walls and phase boundaries, in an array of material systems is now well established. Whilst the existence of conducting interfaces within otherwise insulating mediums is surprising, exciting new avenues for fundamental research have developed, focussing on harnessing the potential for these conducting channels to be active components within nanoscale devices. papers.title: A density functional theory study on the rational design of heterogeneous catalysis
papers.summary: The rational design of efficient catalysts plays a vital and challenging role in heterogeneous catalysis. With the development of computational chemistry techniques, it is realistic to design the desired catalysts by quantum chemical calculations. In this thesis, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to understand the microscopic chemical properties of catalytic systems and the mechanisms of the catalysis, while microkinetic modeling was used to obtain the macroscopic behaviors of the catalytic reactions, which embodied to be the reaction rates. papers.title: A feminine image of the city from Rio de Janeiro’s urban periphery: audiovisual practices, representations and imaginaries
papers.summary: This thesis contends that moving images have an important role in the articulation of society and space, revealing it and shaping it through a connection between the real and the imaginary. Focusing on contemporary production by women from the peripheral region of the Baixada Fluminense, I explore aspects of the relationship between audiovisual practices and representations and the socio-spatial construction of gender in the city, arguing that they embody and make visible an intersectional feminine image of the city. papers.title: Manipulation of the ruminant gastrointestinal tract microbiomes for reduced environmental impact of nitrogen excretion from dairy cows
papers.summary: Nitrogen-use-efficiency (NUE) in dairy production systems remains suboptimal, with higher nitrogen (N) excreted in urine and faeces rather than converted into milk protein. This thesis evaluated nutritional strategies to reduce N excretion and improve NUE without compromising animal performance, to examine the impact of these strategies on the rumen microbiome, while also assessing both local (rapeseed meal: RSM) and novel (microalgae) alternative protein feeds. papers.title: The descendants of Eve: rewriting the Fall in nineteenth-century French literature
papers.summary: This thesis underlines the significance of the French nineteenth-century rewritings of Eve for understanding the contemporary enduring relevance of this rebellious female figure and the lived experience of gender in the twenty-first century. From Balzac’s adulterous housewife, who must be ‘lifted up’ and redeemed, to Villiers de l’Isle Adam’s (dis-)obedient Eve robot, there presentation of Eve takes a plurality of forms in nineteenth-century French literature. papers.title: The interplay among finishing pig nutrition, gut microbiota and the generation of volatile compounds and greenhouse gases
papers.summary: The pork production industry has reached an environmental crisis point, odour and ammonia emissions from pig farms are halting expansion. With pork the second most consumed meat globally, a solution to the demand for cheap and sustainable meat sources must be found. Chapter 2 will investigate dietary manipulation to mitigate these environmental concerns, while Chapters 3 and 4 will focus on odour producing gut microbiota. papers.summary: This study examines the EU’s exercise of maritime security in the Central Mediterranean, within the context of boat migration along this migration route. The focus of the study is upon the role of maritime zones in maritime security implementation and evolution of associated practices. Zonation strategy is coined herein, to characterise the manipulation of maritime zones to align with security and political agendas. papers.title: SmartDecompiler-R1: Enhancing Faithful and Explainable Smart Contract Bytecode Decompilation with Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Understanding EVM bytecode is critical for smart contract security analysis. Existing decompilers typically rely on heuristic rules or leverage large language models (LLMs) to generate source code after bytecode analysis. However, heuristic-based approaches often produce pseudocode that is difficult for humans to interpret, while LLM-based methods also face several problems. LLMs have little experience with low-level bytecode, which weakens their reasoning and causes inaccurate results.
